# Getting Started with R and JupyterLab on DNAnexus

<p class="mcps-home-lead">
A self-paced introduction to the DNAnexus workflow used for R-based analysis in MCPS.
</p>

</div>

</div>

::: {.callout-note title="Who is this for?"}
This tutorial is designed for **MCPS researchers, workshop participants, and collaborators who are new to DNAnexus**.

You might be:

- attending an **MCPS workshop** and using a workshop project; or
- starting work in an **MCPS research project** that you have been given access to.

The tutorial works for both situations.

You do **not** need previous experience with DNAnexus, JupyterLab, cloud computing, or the command line.
:::

## What you will learn

By the end of this tutorial, you will be able to:

- find the DNAnexus project you have been given access to;
- identify where to keep your own work;
- start an R-based JupyterLab environment;
- understand what is saved permanently and what is temporary;
- open and use a persistent **`[DX]` DNAnexus Notebook**;
- read training data stored in your project directly from R;
- save your analysis and its outputs;
- safely terminate your JupyterLab session; and
- return later and continue your work.

## The workflow

The DNAnexus workflow is simple:

1. **Project** — Open the project you have been given access to.
2. **Workspace** — Find the folder where you will keep your own work.
3. **JupyterLab** — Start a temporary computing environment.
4. **`[DX]` Notebook** — Open your persistent notebook.
5. **R analysis** — Read data, analyse, and create outputs.
6. **Save and terminate** — Save your work and stop your computing session.

<div class="mcps-workflow-summary">

**Project → Workspace → JupyterLab → `[DX]` notebook → R analysis → Save → Terminate**

</div>

::: {.callout-warning title="Data safety"}
This tutorial uses **synthetic training data**.

If you are completing the tutorial from a project containing real MCPS research data, **you do not need to use those data at any point in this tutorial**.

Individual-level MCPS research data must remain within the approved DNAnexus environment.

Only download outputs that have been explicitly identified as safe and appropriate to export.
:::

## How to use this tutorial

Work through the sections in order.

The tutorial explains **what to do and why**, while a small `getting-started.ipynb` notebook gives you a place to practise the workflow yourself.

The shared files used for these exercises are kept in a folder called:

```text
mcps-dnanexus-onboarding/
```

We will show you where to find this folder and your own working area before you start JupyterLab.

::: {.callout-tip title="You do not need to memorise the steps"}
The **Quick reference** at the end of the tutorial provides a short version of the workflow that you can return to during future workshops or analyses.
:::
